description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/backend.rs:34-83 (whole trait
docstring is silent on identity); FileNode model in
crate-jmap-filenode-types defines `shareWith` ACLs.

Background: per workspace AGENTS.md "Caller identity (foundation
seam)", `JmapBackend::principal_id(caller: &Self::CallerCtx) ->
Option<&jmap_types::Id>` is the only way for a JMAP method to learn
who the caller is. The trait doc on `principal_id` lists which
extensions need it correct:

> A None-returning backend CANNOT correctly implement chat
> role-hierarchy, calendar ACLs, sharing/myRights, per-user $seen
> on shared mailboxes, or metadata isPrivate visibility scoping.

FileNode is missing from this list. But FileNode HAS sharing
semantics — the `FileNode.shareWith` property (a per-principal ACL
map) is part of the wire shape. A `FileNode/get` call from principal
P should:

- Return only the nodes P has read access to (filtered by shareWith).
- Return the `myRights` derived view (if/when the FileNode draft
  adds it, parallel to RFC 8621 §2 Mailbox.myRights).
- Reject `FileNode/set` updates to nodes P does not have write
  access to.
- Reject `FileNode/copy` operations that read from a fromAccountId
  P cannot see, or write to an accountId P cannot write to.

None of the trait's seven write/structural methods documents how the
backend should consult `principal_id` for these checks. The
`crate-jmap-filenode-server/AGENTS.md` does say:

> Permission enforcement: backend canonical
> The filenode-specific implications: every FileNode mutation must
> be authorized against the caller's effective rights on the parent
> FileNode (RFC 9670 myRights semantics, propagated through
> jmap-sharing-server when present).

…but this is buried in the per-crate AGENTS.md, NOT in the trait
docstring where backend implementors will look. A real-world backend
author reading `pub trait FileNodeBackend` will see seven methods,
none of which mention the principal, and reasonably conclude that
permission checking is the handler's job (which contradicts the
workspace policy that it is the backend's job).

Concrete contract gap: the doc on
`FileNodeBackend::create_object` says "Create a new FileNode."
Nothing about authorization. A backend that follows the trait's
documented contract literally — "if create succeeds, return Ok" —
will permit any caller to create any node anywhere, including in
shared directories the caller has no write access to. That is a
silent privilege-escalation bug rooted in a contract gap, not a
code bug.

Suggested fix: add a header comment block to the trait that

1. References the workspace foundation seam: `principal_id` is the
   only identity surface.
2. States the FileNode-specific implications: shareWith ACLs,
   per-method enforcement (create requires write on the parent,
   update requires write on the target, destroy requires write on
   the target, copy requires read on source and write on destination
   parent).
3. Calls out that the handler library does NO authorization — the
   backend is the canonical enforcement point — and the relationship
   to jmap-sharing-server when present.

Propagation note: every extension-server in the workspace shares
this concern. The canonical jmap-mail-server's trait doc has its
own pass at this (the `isUnread` keyword discussion in the trait
header doc). FileNode's trait doc has zero. Apply the same depth
of contract spec across the sibling family in a single sweep.

`api-contract,underspecified` because the workspace policy
("backend canonical for permission enforcement") is documented in
AGENTS.md but not in the trait's own rustdoc. A backend author who
reads only the rustdoc — the documented contract — will produce
a wrong backend.
title: FileNodeBackend trait doc says nothing about how principal_id maps to FileNode ACL semantics (shareWith)
